key_facts.claim: Self-service erasure is DELETE /users/{ids} (owner or admin) -> UserService.delete -> archiveUser: TO_BE_DELETED, tokenVersion++, save, cache evict. No Firebase, Firestore or Storage call.
Influencer archival only deletes APPLIED applications and nulls email-verification timestamps; the N/A name and phone anonymization exists only for COMPANY. It throws while collaborations are active.

Influencer soft-delete blockers are active applications (ACCEPTED_BY_COMPANY..CONTENT_POSTED_REJECTED; TO_BE_PAID and DONE do not block) plus pending APPLIED; support-ticket and permanent-delete blockers are empty placeholders; DELETE does not re-check eligibility (archiveUser only throws on active collaborations), so the pending-application gate is FE-only.

Nothing purges TO_BE_DELETED: no job sets DELETED, User.deletedAt is never written, TO_BE_DELETED may return to ACTIVE/IN_VALIDATION. DeferredDeletionCronJob loads only PENDING PendingDataDeletionRequest rows (created only by the Meta callback) and itself calls archiveUser.

Meta data-deletion: HMAC-verified signed_request -> connection DISCONNECTED -> archiveUser + COMPLETED row, or TO_BE_DELETED + PENDING row with blockers JSON -> Firestore instagramUsers delete (result ignored). Unknown user or any exception yields a random, unpersisted confirmation code.
Deauthorization: verified email -> DISCONNECTED + Firestore delete + notice email, account kept; unverified -> archiveUser (exceptions swallowed) + Firestore delete.

Hard delete is admin-only and has no FE UI (FE wraps only the partnership-opportunity cascade): delete-permanently = PG delete+flush then Firebase Auth; cascade = applications/history/content, user, Firestore instagramUsers, TOTP+audit, Storage users/{uid}/, Firebase Auth, evict, CascadeDeleteTask with daily retry of FAILED systems.

FK actions decide what a hard delete leaves: consent_record SET NULL; support_ticket (contact_email, ip_address) and search_query_log SET NULL; user_consent and recipient notifications CASCADE; notifications.influencer_id is unkeyed; pending_data_deletion_request has no ON DELETE; applied_opportunity.influencer_id is NOT NULL with ON DELETE SET NULL; file_uploads.user_id is an unkeyed varchar.
RedisUserCache stores only active/role/status/tokenVersion/emailVerified under a hashed UID with a 5-minute TTL; eviction is access revocation, not erasure.

gaps.finding: Erasure requests leave the influencer's PII indefinitely: user row (names, email, phone), addresses, user_social_connection (username, email, picture, followers), Firebase Auth user, Firestore totpSecrets (plus instagramUsers on self-service) and uploads. Meanwhile the UI promises permanent removal, an FE comment claims DeferredDeletionCronJob runs the cascade, and Meta's status reports COMPLETED.

gaps.finding: Cascade Storage cleanup deletes users/{uid}/ but uploads land under content/{userId}/ (prod config; storage rules make them publicly readable), so files survive while the task records SUCCESS; no flow deletes file_uploads rows.

Users who went through Meta deletion cannot be hard-deleted: neither path removes pending_data_deletion_request rows (no-action FK). In forceDeleteUser the user DELETE flushes at commit, after Firestore/Storage/Firebase Auth deletions already ran, so PG rolls back together with the task row while external identities are gone. delete-permanently also fails for any influencer with applications (NOT NULL + SET NULL).

Failures are reported as success: deleteInstagramUserData returns false instead of throwing; cascade maps false to SKIPPED (never retried); Meta services ignore it and log success; callback errors return unpersisted codes; the status URL https://checkitout.app/deletion-status has no FE route (wildcard -> error/404).
Deferred requests can stay PENDING forever: pending APPLIED applications block eligibility although archiveUser would just delete them, and the TO_BE_DELETED influencer cannot log in to withdraw.

Retention is accidental: orphaned consent_record proofs (IP, UA) are purged by the 1-year anonymous-banner cleanup keyed on original timestamp; ConsentSource.ACCOUNT_DELETION is never written; user_consent history cascades away; counterpart notifications keep ActorSnapshot name/avatar by design; support tickets keep contact_email and IP.

invariants: Legally required records survive in minimized, pseudonymized form with explicit retention: consent proofs (document version, timestamp), the erasure request/confirmation log, and billing records (invoice_record is currently ON DELETE CASCADE).
Access is revoked immediately on request (tokenVersion bump + cache eviction) and an erased account can never be reactivated or relinked.
Active collaborations block only the data needed to finish or settle them; counterpart company records stay consistent.
Meta callbacks always answer 200 with a persisted confirmation_code whose status page resolves.

Each external store (Firebase Auth, Firestore instagramUsers/totpSecrets, Storage content/{uid}/, file_uploads) is tracked and retried until verified, never marked done on failure; last-admin protection stays.
good_designs: One server-side erasure state machine (REQUESTED->BLOCKED->SCHEDULED->PURGED) behind self-service, Meta and admin entry points: persist the request, enforce blockers server-side, then after a grace period hard-delete or irreversibly anonymize PG data and run idempotent per-system deletions after commit via an outbox task.
Separate retention from identity: move legally required records to a pseudonymous tombstone with scheduled expiry and scrub counterpart copies (notification snapshots, tickets, search logs) at purge.

Fix the wiring defects first: delete content/{uid}/ and file_uploads, give pending_data_deletion_request a SET NULL/tombstone FK, make application influencer nullable or placeholder, throw on Firestore failure, route /deletion-status.
red_flags: DeferredDeletionCronJob hard-deletes self-service requests (it only re-runs archiveUser for Meta PENDING rows).
archiveUser anonymizes an influencer's name and phone (only handleCompanyArchival does).
Admin cascade delete removes all uploaded files (it deletes users/{uid}/; uploads live under content/{uid}/).
Consent records are deleted with the user (consent_record is SET NULL, then swept by the 1-year anonymous cleanup; only user_consent cascades).
Cascade delete is guarded by a one-time code and the expected entity count (code is deterministic CASCADE-DELETE-{id}; expectedEntityCount is never compared).

architecture.today: Self-service DELETE, Meta callbacks and two crons use checkDeletionEligibilityForUser (DeletionBlocker lists) and archiveUser, which sets TO_BE_DELETED, bumps tokenVersion and evicts the user cache the JWT filter reads.
architecture.fit: Extends these methods (server-side blockers, influencer PII scrub) and ends purges in terminal DELETED, so every entry point erases and revokes alike.
architecture.breaks: A new erasure service, flag or state table beside archiveUser that the cache and filter ignore.

architecture.today: Admin cascade deletes PostgreSQL, Firestore, Storage and Firebase Auth data, tracking SUCCESS/FAILED/SKIPPED per system on CascadeDeleteTask, retried daily by OrphanCleanupTask (max 3, no ShedLock).
architecture.fit: Runs purge side effects as CascadeDeleteTask systems after commit, adding uploads, and marks errors FAILED so they retry.
architecture.breaks: Fire-and-forget external deletes, a new outbox table or broker, or a second retry job.

architecture.pattern: Signed Meta callbacks and deletion requests
architecture.today: Meta callbacks check signed_request by HMAC-SHA256 and always return 200; data-deletion stores PendingDataDeletionRequest rows (code, status, blockers) that DeferredDeletionCronJob rechecks daily under @SchedulerLock.
architecture.fit: Reuses parseSignedRequest and records every erasure request in that table, advanced by the same locked cron.
architecture.breaks: A second signature check, non-200 replies or unpersisted codes, a new request table, or an unlocked scheduler.

architecture.pattern: Liquibase FK actions and consent records
architecture.today: Dated SQL changesets set FK actions (consent_record SET NULL, invoice_record CASCADE) and CHECK enums with consent source ACCOUNT_DELETION; a ShedLock cron purges user-less consent rows after a year.
architecture.fit: Changes retention through new changesets (tombstone, request-row FK, kept invoices) and keeps pseudonymized consent proofs out of the anonymous cleanup.
architecture.breaks: Deleting consent records with the user, editing applied changesets, JPA cascade, or a new audit store.

architecture.today: Uploads go to content/{userId}/ and are tracked in file_uploads (DELETED status exists); FirebaseStorageService.deleteUserDirectory only removes users/{uid}/.
architecture.fit: Deletes the content/{uid}/ blobs listed in file_uploads via FirebaseStorageService and marks the rows, as a cascade system.
architecture.breaks: A new file registry, or storage SUCCESS after deleting users/{uid}/ only.

architecture.pattern: Frontend flow via core API wrappers
architecture.today: Profile deletion goes through UserApiService, a core wrapper over the generated client (check-api-wrappers gate): eligibility, blockers or confirm dialog, DELETE /users/{id}, sign-out.
architecture.fit: A deletion-status page or erasure UI wraps generated clients in core services and leaves blockers to the server.
architecture.breaks: HttpClient or hand-written clients in feature code, or blockers enforced only in the component.
